solution: Rewrite the term with the larger exponent using $a^{m+n}=a^{m}\cdot a^{n}$: ${=b}^{t+1}={=b}^{t}\cdot {=b}$, so the equation becomes ${=b}^{t}+{=b}^{t}\cdot {=b}={=n}$.
Write the right-hand side as a power of ${=b}$: ${=b}^{t}={=b}^{{=e}}$.
The bases are the same, so equate the exponents: $t={=e}$.
notes: Entry point of the skill: two terms, the second exponent exceeds the first by exactly 1, no coefficient. This is the book's ex2-3-1j (2^t + 2^(t+2) = 40) with the shift cut to 1 and the same steps: rewrite, take out the common factor, simplify, write as a power of the same prime base, equate exponents. Parameter space is every (b, e) with b in {2, 3, 5} and e in 2..5 / 2..4 / 2..3, nine instances. I checked all nine by brute force: the left side equals n for exactly one integer t, and that t equals e. Largest n is 750 (5^3 * 6). Numeric answer is a whole number from 2 to 5. No mcq: the book catalogue holds no misconceptions for this objective, and a distractor with no diagnosable error would be padding.
